title: Count of Palindrome Partitions
hints: instead of cutting everywhere and checking afterward, only ever try a cut that makes the current piece a palindrome - this prunes huge parts of the search early
recurse with a start index; at each call, try every end position from start+1 to the end of the string, and only recurse further if s[start:end] is a palindrome
when start reaches the end of the string, you've completed one valid partition - increase your count by 1 and let that branch end (no explicit list needed since you're counting, not collecting)
precomputing which (i, j) substrings are palindromes with a small DP table avoids re-checking palindrome-ness from scratch on every recursive call
commonMistakes: checking palindrome-ness only at the end, on a wide range of arbitrary cuts, instead of pruning as soon as a piece fails to be a palindrome
off-by-one errors on substring bounds when trying each possible end position
forgetting the base case (start reaches string length counts as one valid completed partition, not zero)

content.problemStatement:
You're given a string `s`.

**Count how many different ways you can cut `s` into a sequence of contiguous, non-empty pieces such that every piece, read on its own, is a palindrome.**

Two ways are different if they cut the string at different positions.
constraints: s consists only of lowercase English letters
every piece in a partition must be non-empty and must itself read the same forwards and backwards
notes: string where every character is identical (many valid partitions)
string with no palindromic substring longer than 1 character, other than the whole string possibly not being one either

sampleTestCases.explanation: the two valid partitions are "a"|"a"|"b" and "aa"|"b"
"a"|"a"|"a", "a"|"aa", "aa"|"a", and "aaa" are all valid since any substring of identical characters is a palindrome
only "a"|"b" works, since "ab" itself is not a palindrome
the two valid partitions are "a"|"a"|"b" and "aa"|"b"
"a"|"a"|"a", "a"|"aa", "aa"|"a", and "aaa" are all valid since any substring of identical characters is a palindrome
only "a"|"b" works, since "ab" itself is not a palindrome

optimal.time: O(2^n * n) worst case, but with much of the tree pruned since non-palindromic prefixes are cut off immediately
optimal.space: O(n) recursion depth, plus O(n^2) if you precompute palindrome checks
optimal.pattern: backtracking that only ever extends the current cut with a piece already confirmed to be a palindrome, pruning invalid pieces immediately

bruteForce.approach: try every one of the 2^(n-1) ways to place cuts between characters, and for each, check whether every resulting piece is a palindrome
bruteForce.time: O(2^n * n) (checking each piece for palindrome-ness costs up to O(n))
